title: Outdoor Fitness vs Gym Membership in NZ — Why You Might Not Need Both
meta_desc: Outdoor fitness in NZ vs gym membership: compare prices, contract terms and find the best option for you
intro: With New Zealand's stunning outdoors, many Kiwis are opting for outdoor fitness activities like running and cycling over traditional gym memberships. However, there are scenarios where a gym membership can add value to your fitness routine. Let's explore the reality of outdoor fitness in NZ and when a gym membership might be worth considering.

sections.heading: NZ Outdoor Fitness Reality
sections.body: New Zealand's great outdoors offers plenty of opportunities for physical activity, from hiking and trail running to cycling and water sports. With over 30 percent of Kiwis engaging in outdoor activities at least once a week, it's clear that many prefer the freedom and variety that comes with exercising outside.

sections.heading: Running and Cycling in NZ
sections.body: Running and cycling are two of the most popular outdoor activities in NZ, with many groups and clubs catering to enthusiasts. For example, the Auckland Running Club offers weekly group runs, while the NZ Cycling Federation provides training programs and events for cyclists of all levels.

sections.heading: Outdoor Bootcamps and Group Fitness
sections.body: Outdoor bootcamps and group fitness classes are also gaining popularity in NZ, with many gyms and fitness studios offering outdoor sessions. For instance, Les Mills NZ offers outdoor bootcamps in several locations, including Auckland and Wellington, with prices starting from $15 per session.

sections.heading: When a Gym Membership Adds Value
sections.body: While outdoor fitness activities can be an excellent way to stay active, there are scenarios where a gym membership can add value to your fitness routine. For example, during the winter months when outdoor activities may be limited, a gym membership can provide a convenient and weather-proof alternative. Additionally, gyms often offer specialized equipment and classes that may not be available outdoors.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.body: Ultimately, the decision between outdoor fitness and a gym membership in NZ depends on your individual preferences, fitness goals, and lifestyle. By considering the prices, contract terms, and benefits of each option, you can make an informed decision that suits your needs and budget.
